Remember the Titans is one of those movies that feels even more powerful when you learn how much of it really happened.

The 2000 Disney film was inspired by the true story of the 1971 T.C. Williams High School football team in Alexandria, Virginia. Denzel Washington played Coach Herman Boone, who had to work alongside Bill Yoast as the newly formed team brought players from different schools together during a tense period of racial division. 

And the cast took the football seriously. The young actors were put through an intense training camp before filming, with former players later joking that the workouts nearly broke them. 

But one of the most interesting things is how much Hollywood changed. The real Titans were already an incredibly talented team and finished the season 13–0, while the movie turned their season into a much bigger underdog story. The famous Gettysburg speech, the 3 a.m. run and several other dramatic moments were created for the film. 

Denzel Washington later described the movie perfectly: “I don’t think it’s a football movie.” For him, it was about the potential of the human spirit. 

Even the heartbreaking story of Gerry Bertier was based on real events. The real Bertier was paralyzed in a car accident, although it happened after the championship game rather than before it as shown in the movie. He later competed as a Paralympian.

Hollywood changed plenty of details, but the heart of the story was real: these players came together, won a championship and became an example of what a team could be.

Have you seen Remember the Titans? 🏈
